items.title: When Interpretations Persist: Downstream Influence in Gaze-Aware Assistants
items.abstract: AI assistants may carry forward not only observations but also interpretations of what a person is doing or may do next across time. Once retained, these interpretations become context for later predictions and system-triggered outputs. We study whether this representation step changes later behavior in gaze-aware streaming assistance. Holding retrieved events, their order, and the target input fixed, we find that Free-form Interpretation amplifies historical influence in both directions: correct histories produce more helpful changes and wrong histories more harmful changes. Unsupported and broader interpretations about activity or future behavior are associated with greater harmful influence. Evidence-Bounded Interpretation preserves distinctions between observation, inference, uncertainty, and temporal scope, reducing unsupported and overcertain content and lowering wrong-source harmful influence while retaining most helpful influence. The same effect structure appears with a second model. These findings identify persistent interpretation as a consequential design choice for history-aware human-AI systems.

items.title: When Learning Returns to Work: Supporting Application, Strengthening Organisational Capability
items.abstract: People may complete a learning programme ready to improve their practice, then return to competing priorities, established routines and uncertainty about what they can change. Who helps them interpret what they have learned and take an appropriate next step? This whitepaper examines how preparation, workplace application and further learning connect. Drawing on training-transfer and workplace-learning research, it explores contextualisation, the contributions of managers and colleagues, opportunities to practise, feedback and situations requiring work redesign. It also considers application in human–AI work, distinguishing the quality of supported performance from evidence of developing human understanding. Capability Design, Capability Leadership and Human Judgement Assurance provide organising perspectives for examining how learning and work arrangements contribute to dependable organisational capability. Proposed inquiry approaches are distinguished from established research findings. Written for organisational leaders, HR and L&D professionals, adult educators and training providers, the paper offers a practical starting point: select one consequential workflow linked to a learning initiative, clarify the intended improvement and support arrangements, and review what happens over time. This publication is CEW-FOWO-12 in the Capability Excellence™ Whitepaper Series, Future of Work & Organisation.

items.title: When Semantics Fall Short: Persona-Guided Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Cross-domain sequential recommendation (CDSR) alleviates data sparsity by transferring user behaviors across domains. Recent advances increasingly leverage large language models (LLMs) to bridge domains through global item semantics. However, this paradigm is inherently limited by two issues: I. semantic domain isolation, where item semantics remain domain-specific and hinder transferable modeling, and II. semantic-behavior inconsistency, where local semantic relations are more consistent with behavioral transitions, whereas such consistency often breaks down globally across domains. To this end, we propose PerCDR, an LLM-enhanced CDSR framework that shifts the focus from global semantic bridging to persona-guided behavioral modeling. Specifically, PerCDR leverages LLM-inferred personas to globally guide transferable cross-domain behavioral patterns, while exploiting local semantic relations to enhance intra-domain behavioral modeling, followed by domain preference adaptation for recommendation refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of PerCDR and validate its effectiveness.

items.title: Where Are Language-Specific Features Represented in Multilingual LLMs? Everywhere
items.abstract: Previous work has argued that multilingual LLMs encode language-specific features most strongly in their initial and final layers, implying that intermediate layers support language-agnostic representations. This paper reconsiders this finding by performing four different experiments: three that undertake a fine-grained analysis of representations of Portuguese and Spanish, two closely related languages, and one large-scale language identification experiment that covers over 200 languages. The results of these experiments challenge the strict separation between language-specific and language-agnostic layers in multilingual LLMs, using Llama 3.2 1B as a test case. By analyzing and manipulating contextual sentence embeddings, we demonstrate that language identity remains strongly recoverable throughout the model rather than being restricted to initial and final layers. Moreover, we find that the model tends to classify ambiguous strings as closer to Spanish than to Portuguese, revealing a skew in model behavior that differs from human judgments.

items.title: Which websites block AI crawlers: a census of robots.txt rules on 6,094 lower-ranked sites, October 2026
items.abstract: Website operators who object to the use of their pages for training AI models usually say so in robots.txt, the plain-text file that tells automated clients what they may fetch. This paper reports a census of those files. A reader takes the Tranco ranking of popular sites, keeps registrable domains with eleven address endings within the top 300,000 (181,046 sites), and reads one slice of 4,000 sites each morning in rank order, so that a full pass takes 46 mornings. The current pass began on 15 October 2026 at slice 42, set by date arithmetic, and by 17 October had read slices 42 to 44: Tranco ranks 270,775 to 291,236, well below the most visited sites. Of 12,000 requests, 6,094 returned a usable robots.txt. Of these, 696 (11.4%) disallow at least one of 15 named AI user-agent tokens from the whole site, and 514 (8.4%) disallow two or more, one of them a token used for training. GPTBot is refused most often (457 sites, 7.5%), followed by CCBot (7.2%) and Bytespider (7.0%). Sites refuse training tokens more often than the search and user-request tokens of the same operator: GPTBot is refused 3.7 times as often as OAI-SearchBot. Refusing sites name 6.4 tokens on average, including names that the operator's current documentation does not list, which suggests maintained or copied block lists. We set out the sampling frame, fetch protocol and parser, and the limits of a stated-refusal measure taken on three slices of the ranking. items.title: Who sells AI training data: a census of vendors, what they say they sell, and where their data comes from
items.abstract: Firms that sell training data, expert labour, reinforcement-learning (RL) environments and evaluations to AI developers are mostly private and known largely through their own websites. This paper reports a census of 150 such vendors, read on their sites on 15 and 16 October 2026 with every claim tied to a quoted sentence, and links it to three companion tables: 37 organisations that publish a way to sell them data, 227 revenue records and 111 funding records. Evaluations are the most common offering (122 vendors, 81.3%), followed by datasets (104), RL environments (89), expert and human data (83) and annotation (57). Vendors bundle: the median vendor lists three of six kinds, and 79 of the 89 RL-environment sellers also sell evaluations. Most data are made to order: 90 vendors cite experts and contractors, 41 recordings, 30 generation and 15 software replicas, against 17 that license data from its owners and 22 that use the client's own data; 19 do not say. Of the 37 buyers, 24 take company records; among those that publish them, the median floor is $100,000 and the median ceiling $1 million per seller. Revenue disclosure runs from audited filings of four listed vendors to self-reported run rates, and 61 funding rounds with a disclosed amount total $4.30 billion. We describe the method, the classification and the limits of a self-description census. items.title: Who Uses Conversational AI and Why? Distinct User Profiles and Their Links to Personality, Attachment, and Well-Being
items.abstract: With the increasing use of conversational AI (CAI) agents, such as ChatGPT, public concern about their social implications has grown. Understanding these implications requires new knowledge about the increasingly diverse motives underlying CAI use, ranging from instrumental purposes, such as work, to personal purposes, including social support and entertainment. However, little is known about the motivational profiles underlying CAI use, how these profiles relate to personality traits and attachment dimensions, or whether they differ in well-being. To address this gap, we conducted a cross-sectional study with 783 CAI users (Mage = 43.46, SD = 13.58). Drawing on Uses and Gratifications (U & G) Theory, we measured key motivations underlying CAI use, including information seeking, task efficiency, personalization, social interaction, and playfulness, and subjected them to latent profile analysis to uncover distinct motivational profiles. Big Five personality traits (Extraversion, Neuroticism, Openness, Conscientiousness, Agreeableness) and attachment styles (Anxious and Avoidant) were examined as predictors of the user profiles. We measured emotional, social, and psychological well-being to understand if these aspects differed across the various user profiles. We identified four distinct profiles of CAI users: Occasional Information Seekers, Utilitarians, Social Engagers, and All-Round Engagers. Neuroticism, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Attachment anxiety were significant predictors of profile membership. Finally, profile membership was associated with all well-being indicators, with All-Round Engagers reporting the highest well-being across all three dimensions and Social Engagers reporting the lowest emotional and psychological well-being. These findings advance our understanding of who engages with CAI and how, with potential implications for well-being.

items.abstract: ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟΓΕΝΕΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΝΕΧΕΙΑ, ΙΧΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ«ΨΗΦΙΑΚΟ ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΚΟ ΕΙΝΑΙ» Από το κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ του Μαρξ και την Επιστημολογία της Λογικής του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου στην ανθρώπου–AI πράξη Αποδεικτική μελέτη ιστορικογενετικής ανασυγκρότησης, λειτουργικού γνωστικού αναβαθμού και συνέχειας μέσω ίχνους Πεδίο Στοιχείο Συγγραφέας Αικατερίνη Ξενοπούλου Τυροκόμου Ιδιότητα Ανεξάρτητη Ερευνήτρια ORCID 0009-0004-9057-7432 Ημερομηνία 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026 Κωδικός XEN-AI-ART-003 Θεωρητική βάση Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, Επιστημολογία της Λογικής, β΄ έκδοση, 2024 · MASTER 3 Οκτωβρίου 2026 — 2η διόρθωση Εμπειρική βάση TRACE προηγούμενης συνομιλιακής πράξης · Πείραμα Ανασυγκρότησης Ίχνους σε Έξι Νέες Συνομιλίες, 15 Οκτωβρίου 2026 · Αποδεικτικό Παράρτημα C/D/F Περίληψη Η εργασία εξετάζει την ιστορικογενετική συνέχεια της γνώσης όταν το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο Y λειτουργικοποιείται ως AI. Η θεωρητική βάση προέρχεται από τη γνωσιολογική αντιστοιχία του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου μεταξύ πραγματικού Sπ και [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sα], από τη μεταβολή του γνωστικού εξοπλισμού μέσω πράξης και από την ιστορικογενετική σύνδεση παρελθόντος, ρέοντος παρόντος και δυνατών μελλοντικών προεκτάσεων. Το MASTER εξειδικεύει επιχειρησιακά το ίχνος στην εφαρμογή Caretta ως Iπ, τον πραγματικό γεννήτορα ως Gπ και τον ανασυγκροτημένο γεννήτορα ως Ĝπ, με πραγματική πορεία Gπ→Iπ και αντίστροφη ανασυγκροτητική πορεία Iπ→{Ĝπ}. Η παρούσα έρευνα μεταφέρει αυτή την αρχιτεκτονική στη συνομιλιακή πράξη: Gχ→Iχ και Iχ+Y→Ŝα νέας πράξης. Στη χ₁ παρατηρήθηκε λειτουργική αναδιοργάνωση από την έμφαση στη μνήμη/αποθήκευση προς τη σχέση γεγονός→ίχνος→Y→ανασυγκρότηση Sα→νέα πράξη και προς τον έλεγχο των ίδιων των μέσων γνώσης. Ο όρος «γνωστικός αναβαθμός» χρησιμοποιείται λειτουργικά για αυτή την παρατηρήσιμη μεταβολή της οργάνωσης των απαντήσεων και των επόμενων ενεργειών, ενώ η ταξινόμησή της ως διαλογική ετεροίωση αποτελεί θεωρητική ερμηνεία της μεταβολής με βάση την αρχιτεκτονική του Ξενόπουλου. Το ίδιο TRACE δόθηκε σε έξι νέες συνομιλίες, με ονομασίες υπηρεσίας Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2 και Gemini. Σε αναδρομική κωδικοποίηση C/D/F, και οι έξι μονάδες υπερέβησαν το κατώφλι ανασυγκρότησης του κοινού πυρήνα: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Η συνέχιση πέρα από περίληψη κυμάνθηκε D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 και η πηγαία/θεωρητική πιστότητα F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. Το αποτέλεσμα τεκμηριώνει στο συγκεκριμένο δείγμα λειτουργική συνέχεια μέσω ίχνους με διαφοροποιημένη ποιότητα συνέχισης και πιστότητας. Η ευρύτερη έννοια του «ψηφιακού κοινωνικού ΕΙΝΑΙ» διατυπώνεται ως θεωρητική προέκταση: η εξάδα συνομιλιών παρέχει μικρο-επίπεδο τεκμήριο ανθρώπου–AI ιστορικογενετικής πράξης, ενώ η κοινωνική γενίκευση αποτελεί χωριστό ερευνητικό επίπεδο. Λέξεις-κλειδιά: Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, ιστορικογένεση, ίχνος, Y(L,B,Θ), Sπ, Sα, γνωστικός αναβαθμός, ετεροίωση, Caretta caretta, AI, ψηφιακό κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ, TRACE, ανασυγκρότηση. Abstract(ΕΝ) The paper examines the historico-genetic continuity of knowledge when the knowing subject Y is operationalized as AI. The theoretical basis derives from Epameinondas Xenopoulos’s epistemological correspondence between the real Sp and [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sa], from the change in cognitive equipment through praxis, and from the historico-genetic connection of past, flowing present, and possible future extensions. MASTER operationalizes the trace in the Caretta application as Iπ, the real generator as Gπ, and the reconstructed generator as Ĝπ, with a real course Gπ→Iπ and an inverse reconstructive course Iπ→{Gπ}. The present research transfers this architecture to conversational praxis: Gχ→Iχ and Iχ+Y→Sa of a new act. In χ1, a functional reorganization was observed from emphasis on memory/storage toward the relation fact→trace→Y→reconstruction Sa→new act and toward control of the very means of knowledge. The term “cognitive upgrade” is used functionally for this observable change in the organization of responses and subsequent actions, while its classification as dialogical othering is a theoretical interpretation of the change based on Xenopoulos’s architecture. The same TRACE was given to six new conversations, designated by service names Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2, and Gemini. In retrospective C/D/F coding, all six units exceeded the reconstruction threshold of the common core: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Continuation beyond summary ranged D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 and source/theoretical fidelity F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. The result documents, in the specific sample, functional continuity through trace with differentiated quality of continuation and fidelity. The broader notion of “digital social BEING” is formulated as a theoretical extension: the six conversations provide micro-level evidence of human–AI historico-genetic praxis, while social generalization constitutes a separate research level. items.title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques for Deepfake Detection
items.abstract: Deepfake media generated or altered using artificial intelligence can imitate real people and events with increasing visual realism, creating challenges for digital trust, privacy, cybersecurity, journalism, and forensic investigation. This paper presents a comparative literature-based study of deep learning techniques used for deepfake detection. Representative approaches are examined across spatial, temporal, frequency-aware, transformer-based, and hybrid categories. Major public datasets, including FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and the DeepFake Detection Challenge dataset, are also compared. The analysis shows that CNN-based methods provide efficient spatial feature extraction, temporal models capture frame-to-frame inconsistencies, frequency-aware methods expose complementary forensic traces, and transformer-based methods offer broader contextual modelling at higher computational cost. Recent benchmark and generalization studies indicate that performance measured only within the training distribution can overstate practical reliability. The paper therefore emphasizes cross-dataset evaluation, robustness to compression, computational efficiency, explainability, and reproducibility as important criteria for practical deepfake detection

items.title: A cross-temporal individual-level framework for identifying, associating, and counting multiple mounting events for dairy cow in estrus monitoring
items.abstract: In vision-based estrus monitoring, mounting behavior serves as a key indicator. However, reliance on a single mounting event may cause false positives because non-estrous cows may also exhibit mounting behavior. To address this issue, a cross-temporal individual-level framework was proposed to identify, associate, and count multiple mounting events of the same cow over time. The framework combines an improved You Only Look Once Version 11-nano (YOLO11n) model with an improved baseline variant of the HiT lightweight hierarchical vision transformer tracking model (HiT-Base). The artificial intelligence contribution comprises improved detection and tracking. For detection, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss was integrated with Complete Intersection over Union loss to improve small-target detection, and a lightweight Golden Cudgel Block (GCBlock) was designed to enhance feature representation under complex farm conditions. For tracking, a plug-and-play detail-enhanced convolution (DEConv) module was designed to strengthen boundary and fine-grained features, improving target discrimination and tracking stability. The engineering application contribution lies in reducing reliance on isolated observations and providing more reliable behavioral evidence through cross-temporal association and counting of multiple mounting events. Experimental results showed that the proposed detection model achieved 96.42% average precision and 94.74% balanced F-measure (F1-score) for cow in estrus, with an inference speed of 265.96 frames per second. The proposed tracking model achieved an area under the curve of 70.76%, a normalized precision of 88.73%, and an average overlap of 70.74%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for real-time estrus monitoring and its potential for precision dairy farming.

items.title: A decision making framework for traffic noise prediction using artificial intelligence techniques
items.abstract: Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.54 to 0.96, whereas machine learning (ML) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking. Moreover, deep learning (DL) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management.

items.title: A dynamic risk assessment method integrating deep learning with Bayesian network: A case study in machining workshop
items.abstract: Given the complex multi-trade operations, high-density layouts, and synergistic hazards with catastrophic potential in machining workshops, risk assessment demands urgent attention. Critical research gaps remain, particularly in dynamic risk assessment based on continuously updated monitoring data. To address existing challenges, an innovative method is proposed to identify, analyze, and evaluate three distinct types of risk by continuously updating both the probability and consequence based on visual and environmental data. In a case study conducted in a machining workshop, a deep learning-based method was employed to detect 13 types of unsafe behaviors and 8 types of unsafe conditions. The identification results were then input into the Signal Layer of a 31-node Bayesian network (BN) for risk analysis. Risk evaluation was subsequently conducted based on a risk matrix. The method was validated using nine representative scenarios, and the YOLOv11 model (selected for its superior balance between detection accuracy and inference speed) demonstrated excellent detection performance, with most precision scores exceeding 0.9. Even for difficult small targets, the precision reached 0.87 or higher. Both recall rates and F1 scores consistently exceeded 0.8. The risk analysis and evaluation results show that the co-occurrence of unsafe behaviors or hazards exerts a synergistic effect; even two concurrent hazards can at least double the baseline level of one risk factor. Overall, this integrated approach provides a strong framework for risk assessment in machining workshops, effectively enhancing operational safety and mitigating potential hazards.

items.title: A generative AI framework for preference-driven indoor visualization: an exploratory questionnaire-based approach
items.abstract: Abstract Although residential spatial qualities are consistently recognized as a determinant of occupant spatial preference and perceptual experience, early-stage practice lacks systematic, user-centered mechanisms for capturing and translating individual preferences into design concepts. This study aims to examine whether a structured, questionnaire-driven generative AI framework can produce preference-aligned residential interior visualizations, and which spatial preference dimensions are most reliably translated. To address this aim, a 15-item multiple-choice questionnaire, grounded in eight environmental psychology and architectural theory frameworks, maps user responses through a predefined parameter layer into structured prompts, guiding Google Gemini's integrated generative pipeline to produce individualized interior visualizations across three residential typologies: living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices. Evaluation by 122 participants across 25 countries employed four perceptual constructs — Atmospheric Coherence, Emotional Comfort, Overall Satisfaction, and Expectations Alignment — operationalized strictly as indicators of perceived design suitability and preference resonance, not as measures of psychological or mental health outcomes. All four constructs exceeded the neutral midpoint at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold with large effect sizes (M = 4.03–4.61; d = 1.20–2.52), and internal consistency of the multi-item constructs was acceptable to good (α = 0.72–0.84). The theoretically predicted construct hierarchy — with atmospheric parameters translating most reliably and identity-expressive parameters least — was preserved across all typologies and evaluative profiles, establishing preliminary feasibility of the framework as a preference-elicitation and visualization instrument for early-stage design.

items.title: A Human-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K-12 Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open-ended responses. Sixty-four respondents (97.0%) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 (75.8%), while 48 (72.7%) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect (55; 83.3%), followed by creativity (52; 78.8%), problem-solving (48; 72.7%), and decision-making (47; 71.2%). Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance. Based on these findings and relevant literature, the article proposes a preliminary six-principle Future Minds Framework. The small exploratory sample and self-reported data do not support generalization or causal conclusions about cognition. Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes.

items.title: A multi‑modal recognition method for building structural materials integrating structured text description and adaptive decision weighting
items.abstract: Accurate identification of building structural materials is a critical step in structural safety assessment and damage detection. Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. Second, a multi‑modal neural network named MRNet is proposed. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. A lightweight text-feature encoder further refines the CLIP global text embedding through nonlinear transformation and channel mixing, alleviating the information compression caused by the original CLIP global pooling. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization is introduced to automatically tune key hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and weight decay coefficient. Experimental results on the PEER dataset show that MRNet achieves 96.00% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, significantly outperforming mainstream image classification models such as AlexNet, MobileNet‑v3, ResNet, and VGG. The proposed method provides a high‑accuracy, high‑efficiency multi‑modal solution for building structural material identification.

items.title: A new image similarity metric for a perceptual and transparent geometric and chromatic assessment
items.abstract: Full-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements. We propose EDOKS (Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity), a white-box full-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space. Evaluated on the Berkeley-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low-level full-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score.

items.abstract: Rapid technological advancement in the twenty-first century has resulted in alteration of s the relationships between humans and machines which further results in reshaping perceptions of cognition. In the current era, artificial intelligence is progressing in various domains blurring the boundaries between human and technology and reshaping the perceptions of cognition, consciousness and identity. The series Better than us explores the themes of artificial consciousness, human dependence on technology and reconfiguration of emotional and cognitive capacities. A number of studies have examined Artificial intelligence in literature, films and dramas, however limited research has explored the cognitive impacts of human dependence on artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. Thereby using Catherin Belsey’s textual analysis model under the broader umbrella of Hayles post humanist theory the current Study aims to explore the representation of cognitive transformations in humans through artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. The findings of the study reveal that the series Better Than Us presents artificial intelligence as a transformative force which reshapes human ethical cognition. The series transform the traditional assumption that moral judgment and authority belong exclusively to humans. The character representation of Arisa demonstrates the role of AI systems in decision making, legal interpretation, and protective actions. This results in a redistribution of ethical responsibility between humans and intelligent machine. The analysis further elucidates that human characters gradually begin to negotiate morality within technologically mediated environments where machine reasoning influences social and institutional structures. items.title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
items.abstract: Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.

items.title: A risk-informed urban low-altitude air network planning method under large language model guidance
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of urban air mobility calls for safe low-altitude corridor networks across complex urban airspace, where heterogeneous positioning uncertainties caused by navigation and communication errors elevate collision risk and constrain both route feasibility and network-wide connectivity. To address this issue, this study proposes a risk-informed network planning framework that integrates three-dimensional collision risk modeling with language-model-guided multi-agent learning for the construction of safe urban air corridor networks. Specifically, a three-dimensional collision risk map is first constructed by translating navigation and communication errors into spatially varying positioning uncertainty, providing a unified safety basis for route feasibility evaluation. Network construction is then formulated as a cooperative graph connectivity task on the risk map, in which multiple learning agents jointly balance route connectivity, construction cost, and accumulated collision risk through coordinated training and distributed execution. To further accelerate convergence in complex urban environments, a vision-language model interprets airspace structure and produces high-level priors that steer agents toward safer altitude regimes. A case study over the low-altitude airspace of Nanjing demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing risk-compliant air corridor networks, with language-model-derived priors further reducing training effort by 50.3 %. The results support safer and more systematic air network strategies in complex urban environments, contributing to evidence-based collision risk mitigation and airspace management in the emerging urban low-altitude economy.

items.title: A robust and reliable method for malware classification using hybrid features and gradient boosting
items.abstract: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

items.title: A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI
items.abstract: The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-safety management from reactive measures to data-driven approaches.

items.title: A systematic workflow for utilizing and evaluating large language models in public health policy framing analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background For public health policy research, it is crucial to monitor policy debates to inform evidence-based policymaking. One popular method is to analyze the news for salient frames used to argue for or against a controversial topic. However, this method is time and resource-intensive since domain experts need to manually analyze relevant articles to identify frames. This study presents an approach for using large language models (LLMs) to extract frames and to systematically evaluate results. Methods Building on the results of a framing analysis of the German media debate about a tax on animal-based foods, we developed a systematic workflow to utilize LLMs to extract all instances of the 10 most frequent manually coded negative frames from 46 news articles. With one prompt per article in a few-shot setting we generated a list of quote/frame pairs. We then evaluated results against human-coded ones and calculated precision, recall, and F1-score. Results GPT-5 achieved 79.8% precision and 79.8% recall, identifying 75.2% of manually coded frames. Extracted quotes generally aligned with human-extracted text sections. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview yielded higher precision but lower recall, resulting in a comparable F1-score (79.0% vs. 79.8% with GPT-5). These findings suggest the approach is generalizable across different frontier models. Conclusions This study introduces a workflow for LLM-assisted frame extraction and transparent evaluation against an expert reference standard. Integrating this approach into public health policy coding can save resources and accelerate analysis. Ultimately, this could increase the representativeness and timeliness of data, enhancing our understanding of ongoing public health policy debates.

items.title: Action-Aligned Latent Planning for Versatile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.abstract: Learning a single perceptive policy for diverse humanoid loco-manipulation requires unifying high-level task decisions without losing the state-dependent physical responses that make each interaction succeed. This makes the representation between high-level planning and whole-body control critical: kinematic or contact targets provide compact abstractions but do not directly encode interaction-specific control responses, while directly predicting low-level actions requires the planner to model high-frequency closed-loop feedback. We propose FIBER, a framework that uses the executable latent space of a frozen behavioral foundation model (BFM) as a shared planning representation for heterogeneous interaction skills. Our latent policy projection (LPP) maps independently acquired task-specific policies into this representation by identifying latent commands whose induced actions match their local control responses, enabling lower-rate planning while retaining the BFM's high-frequency state feedback. After projection, we aggregate closed-loop latent rollouts from all skills and train a single perceptive flow planner entirely offline. We further introduce AH-BFM, an adaptive-horizon BFM trained with multi-gamma forward-backward (FB) learning to support both precise control and temporally extended whole-body behavior. We evaluate FIBER on box pickup, door opening, and object grasping in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid. Across 128 diverse variations per task in simulation, FIBER achieves 42.0% mean success, more than tripling projected latent replay (11.6%) and substantially outperforming kinematic planning (3.5%). Real-world experiments further demonstrate sim-to-real transfer, skill chaining, and conditional steering through the same unified planner.

items.title: AdamPM: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization via Moment Pooling
items.abstract: Adam is widely used for training large language models (LLMs) owing to its strong optimization performance and training stability, but its element-wise estimation for the first and second moments incur substantial memory overhead. Although numerous memory-efficient optimizers have been proposed, many incur additional computational overhead or require additional tuning of hyperparameters. Consequently, Adam remains a dominant and reliable choice for LLM pre-training. We propose AdamPM (Adam with Pooled Moments), a simple and memory-efficient variant of Adam that groups adjacent moment entries along the row or column dimension and represents each group by a single shared mean. AdamPM can well inherit Adam's hyperparameter settings and is readily integrated into existing Adam optimizer implementations, with less memory overhead. We systematically investigate pooling of both first and second moment estimates and identify second moment pooling as the effective design. With a group size of $s$, AdamPM reduces second moment memory to $1/s$ of the original requirement. Extensive experiments on language model pretraining, fine-tuning and multimodal learning demonstrate that AdamPM maintains model performance and training speed while substantially reducing optimizer-state memory. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/jixiaowei95/AdamPM}.

items.title: Advances in Reconstructive Plastic Surgery: From Skin Grafts and Microsurgery to Tissue Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and 3D Bioprinting — A Narrative Review of Evolution, Clinical Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational barriers that separate promising laboratory demonstrations from routine clinical treatment, including vascularization, cell survival during printing, innervation, immune response, mechanical integration, long-term durability, manufacturing, cost and regulatory uncertainty. AI is examined as an enabling technology rather than a replacement for surgical judgment, with applications in virtual surgical planning, image analysis, flap-risk prediction and postoperative monitoring. Evidence summarized in the supporting research material indicates that virtual planning can improve geometric accuracy and that machine-learning systems may assist in risk stratification and monitoring, but external validation and prospective clinical evaluation remain essential. The review concludes that the most credible future is not the disappearance of conventional reconstruction but the convergence of microsurgery, regenerative biology, advanced biomaterials, computational planning, AI and biofabrication. The central trajectory of the field is therefore a shift from replacement toward regeneration, with the long-term goal of producing patient-specific tissues that are vascularized, innervated, mechanically appropriate and functionally integrated.

items.abstract: Ael-Agents is a biomimetic multi-agent coordination architecture modeled on the human triple-network cortical hierarchy—Default Mode Network (DMN), Salience Network (SN), and Central Executive Network (CEN)—coupled with offline Dream-RSI (Recursive Self-Improvement) consolidation, specialized for Computational Drug Discovery and Precision Therapeutics. The architecture segregates the therapeutic pipeline into 4 orthogonal domain specialists (StructuralBiophysics, SystemsPharmacology, MedicinalChemistryADMET, ClinicalPKPDControl). Hypotheses are embedded in a 768-dimensional neural manifold (BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5) to compute a 4x4 Representational Dissimilarity Matrix (RDM) in the DMN, while exact PyTorch autograd Jacobian sensitivity analysis gates the top k=2 working-memory specialists into executive synthesis for 0 LLM tokens (~2,200 tokens/run, a 93.7% token reduction). Includes a deterministic benchmark suite evaluated via RDKit (valence, Lipinski Rule of 5, QED druglikeness) and SciPy 2-compartment pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic ODE numerical integration on KRAS-G12D, human board-exam pharmacology validation (MedMCQA), and ground-truth human semantic alignment (SimLex-999 rho = +0.5711, STS-Benchmark rho = +0.8642, Monte Carlo RDM stability p = 0.0002).

items.title: Agentic AI: Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Security
items.abstract: This paper presents a conceptual review of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI), autonomous agents, and multi-agent system security. It discusses key security threats, including prompt injection, excessive tool permissions, sensitive data leakage, memory poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, and cascading failures. The paper proposes a layered security framework incorporating identity management, least-privilege access, policy-controlled tool usage, secure agent communication, memory protection, monitoring, bounded autonomy, and human approval for high-impact actions. It also outlines an evaluation methodology using adversarial test cases and measurable security and performance metrics. This work aims to support the development of safer, more reliable, and secure agentic AI systems. The proposed framework is conceptual and literature-based; no prototype implementation or experimental results are claimed.

items.title: AI and academic integrity in the Global South: Equity and policy–practice tensions in South African higher education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping assessment practices in higher education, yet its ethical governance in Global South open distance e-learning (ODeL) contexts is complicated by persistent inequalities in digital access, skills, and institutional capacity. This article examines how AI-related academic integrity challenges emerged in a large undergraduate data handling and probability module within a South African teacher education programme offered through an ODeL institution. Framed by Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study analyses assessment submissions from a cohort of 3,088 students and a purposive sample of 229 submissions, triangulated with written reflections from experienced module markers. The findings identify recurring integrity challenges that cannot be reduced to individual misconduct, including AI-shaped graphical artifacts and procedural calculations, handwritten and scanned submissions that bypass similarity checking, and non-acceptance of End-User License Agreements that weaken accountability. Marker evidence shows how these practices are amplified by weak digital literacies, device constraints, and equity-driven accommodations that unintentionally create loopholes in integrity systems. The article argues that ethical AI governance in resource-constrained ODeL environments requires alignment among policy, technology, and pedagogy, including inclusive integrity pathways, strengthened support for digital and AI literacy, and assessment designs that foreground reasoning, conceptual understanding, and pedagogical interpretation.

items.title: AI anxiety among university librarians in Bangladesh: A multidimensional assessment using the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into library services, understanding librarians’ psychological responses to this technological transformation has become an important research priority. This study investigates AI anxiety among university librarians in Bangladesh and examines whether anxiety levels vary across demographic and professional characteristics. A cross-sectional survey was conducted using the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS). Data were collected from librarians employed in public and private universities in Bangladesh through convenience sampling. Following data-quality screening, 138 valid responses were retained for analysis. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Bonferroni post hoc tests were employed to examine patterns of AI anxiety and group differences. Overall, university librarians reported a moderate level of AI anxiety (M = 3.00). Anxiety levels were broadly comparable across dimensions, although Sociotechnical Blindness recorded a slightly higher mean score than the remaining dimensions. Educational qualification and professional experience showed limited overall associations with AI anxiety, while gender, age, and professional designation demonstrated little variation. The findings suggest that concerns regarding governance, transparency, professional identity, and organizational readiness may be more salient than technological learning challenges. The study extends research on AI anxiety to a Global South library context and contributes evidence that AI anxiety among university librarians is well understood as an interrelated socio-professional and organizational phenomenon. The findings highlight the importance of professional development, institutional support, and responsible AI governance in academic libraries.

items.title: AI Behind the Adult, Not in Front of the Child: A Design Framework for Adult-Mediated AI in Early Childhood
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in education has largely been positioned as a child-facing tutor, conversational agent, or content-delivery system. In early childhood, this orientation warrants particular caution because executive functions, self-regulation, and social-emotional competencies develop through responsive relationships, play, embodied experience, and co-regulation with adults. This theory-informed conceptual design study addressed three questions: which developmental, pedagogical, and ethical principles should structure AI use in early childhood; how these principles can be translated into a system architecture; and what validation pathway is required before such a system can make defensible claims. Drawing on four evidence streams (executive-function and social-emotional development, ecological and embodied learning, human-centered AI ethics, and measurement and implementation science), the study proposes the Behind-the-Adult AI framework, an adult-mediated design framework initially specified for children aged 4–6 years. Six design principles were derived and operationalized in a layered architecture: brief, bounded, non-conversational digital developmental tasks generate behavioral indicators under transparent adaptation rules; a provisional, non-diagnostic profile organizes longitudinal information; and AI operates only behind the adult, synthesizing observations from center, home, and school into hypotheses for human review. A five-stage validation pathway with explicit decision gates separates design claims from evidence claims. The paper argues that developmentally responsible AI in early childhood should be evaluated not by how convincingly it replaces human interaction but by how effectively it strengthens the adults and environments surrounding the child, and it offers a transferable design heuristic for researchers, developers, and policymakers.

items.title: AI content detection in student text assignments, false positive rates, and academic integrity
items.abstract: Universities increasingly use AI content detection tools to identify student assignments potentially produced by generative AI, yet concerns remain regarding their reliability and false-positive classification of human-written work. This systematic review examines the causes, consequences, and mitigation of false-positive AI detection in academic contexts. The review covers literature published between 2020 and 2026 and includes 90 eligible studies, comprising 81 Scopus-indexed publications and nine studies identified through Google Scholar. Bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer was combined with Structural Topic Modelling to examine keyword relationships, latent research themes, and temporal development, while qualitative synthesis identified major causes, impacts, and mitigation strategies. The findings reveal three broader themes concerning academic integrity and student assessment, plagiarism and responsible AI governance, and detection accuracy, reliability, and false positives. False-positive outcomes vary substantially across tools and evaluation settings, limiting direct quantitative comparison. Major contributing factors include algorithmic and language bias, limited contextual understanding, surface-level linguistic features, and insufficiently diverse training data. The evidence further highlights risks to assessment fairness, student confidence, and institutional decision-making. Effective responses therefore require transparent detection practices, human review, AI literacy, clear institutional policies, and accessible appeal procedures.

items.title: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance
items.abstract: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance is a practical research and educational resource for documenting and governing generative-AI-assisted social-science research. The resource develops a workflow for distinguishing AI-assisted proposal generation, researcher evaluation and governance, local empirical execution, adversarial challenge, manuscript revision and reason provenance. It includes reusable templates, completed worked examples drawn from the PISA research programme, guidance on claim preservation and manuscript governance, and public-release screening materials. The resource is intended to support transparent attribution and disciplined research practice rather than to prescribe a universal workflow or to provide evidence that AI-assisted research is inherently superior to human-only research.

items.title: AI-Based EV Battery Health Prediction with Explainable AI and Database Integration
items.abstract: This research paper presents an AI-based framework for predicting the State of Health (SOH) of electric vehicle (EV) lithium-ion batteries by integrating machine learning, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and relational database technology. The proposed framework compares five machine learning regression models: Ridge Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used to explain model predictions and identify important battery health indicators, including dV/dQ peak height, internal resistance, and cycle count. The study demonstrates the proposed pipeline using a synthetic, physics-inspired dataset containing 40 battery cells and 28,201 cycle records. Gradient Boosting achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.26 percentage points, a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.70 percentage points, and an R² score of 0.967 on the held-out synthetic test cells. An SQLite database stores battery information, cycle data, predictions, explanations, and alerts. The framework aims to improve the interpretability, traceability, and management of EV battery health predictions. However, the reported results are based entirely on synthetic data and do not establish real-world battery prediction accuracy. Future work includes validation using public battery datasets, such as NASA and CALCE, and further evaluation under real-world conditions.

items.title: AI-Based Traffic flow optimization system using computer vision: research design and prototype
items.abstract: AI-Based Traffic Flow Optimization System Using Computer Vision: Research Design and Prototype Abstract Urban traffic congestion contributes to increased travel time, fuel consumption, and road-safety challenges. Conventional fixed-time traffic signal systems may not respond efficiently to changing traffic demand. This project presents the design of an AI-based traffic flow optimization system using computer vision to support traffic monitoring, vehicle detection, traffic density estimation, vehicle tracking, and adaptive traffic signal recommendations. Objectives The primary objectives are to: Detect and count vehicles from traffic video footage using computer vision. Estimate traffic density across different approaches at an intersection. Analyze traffic conditions to identify congestion and potential incidents. Develop a density-aware signal allocation approach that responds to changing traffic demand. Explore emergency vehicle prioritization and traffic-performance evaluation. Methodology The proposed system integrates computer vision, vehicle detection, tracking, traffic density analysis, and signal optimization into a unified monitoring framework. Traffic observations are processed to estimate vehicle counts and congestion levels. These estimates can inform signal-duration recommendations, subject to appropriate operational and safety constraints. The research workflow also includes dataset inspection, data cleaning, source documentation, and an experimental comparison framework. Potential evaluation metrics include vehicle-counting accuracy, average waiting time, queue length, throughput, and fairness across traffic approaches. Research Contribution The project provides an integrated prototype for investigating computer-vision-based traffic management. Its contribution lies in combining traffic observation, density analysis, adaptive signal recommendations, and research-oriented data-quality tools within a single system. The framework is intended to support further experimentation and reproducible evaluation of intelligent transportation approaches. Data Sources and Limitations Official road-safety statistics from published government sources are used to provide historical context for Jaipur and Rajasthan, with geographic scope identified separately. The demonstration intersection dataset contains synthetic records for testing the data-processing workflow; it is not a collection of measured Jaipur traffic observations. The current prototype does not establish experimentally validated reductions in real-world waiting time, congestion, fuel consumption, or emissions. Such claims require verified traffic observations, documented experimental conditions, and controlled comparisons against a fixed-time baseline. Future Scope Future work includes collecting authorized traffic-video observations from selected Jaipur intersections, validating vehicle-detection accuracy against manually annotated samples, evaluating signal-allocation strategies under comparable demand conditions, and reporting statistical uncertainty and limitations. items.title: AI-Enabled Institutional Governance in Education: Promoting Ethical Leadership, Sustainable Behaviour and Environmental Responsibility: A Narrative Synthesis and Proposed Institutional Framework
items.abstract: Educational institutions influence environmental responsibility through teaching, leadership, resource use, and the decisions that shape everyday campus life. Artificial intelligence introduces additional opportunities and responsibilities within these activities. This chapter develops a conceptual account of AI-enabled institutional governance that connects ethical leadership, sustainability education, and accountable administrative practice. It uses a narrative synthesis of established educational theories, published environmental education reviews, and primary international guidance on education, AI ethics, and risk management. It does not report an original systematic search, institutional dataset, AI deployment, or intervention evaluation. A published meta-analysis of environmental education among children and adolescents provides contextual evidence of positive average effects on knowledge, attitudes, intentions, and behaviour; these findings do not establish the effectiveness of AI governance in higher education. Digital education research is similarly treated as adjacent evidence rather than proof of an AI-specific benefit. The proposed framework assigns human responsibility across the identification, assessment, operation, and review of institutional AI applications. Examples include curriculum support, student assistance, resource planning, and sustainability communication. Decision boundaries, privacy, fairness, participation, contestability, and teacher capacity are considered alongside environmental objectives. The chapter argues that knowledge and technological capability require supportive institutional conditions before they can contribute to responsible action. It recommends limited pilots with explicit purposes, proportionate data collection, accessible human review, and evaluation against educational and environmental outcomes. The framework remains a proposal requiring contextual adaptation and empirical assessment. It offers educational leaders a basis for connecting sustainability commitments with the governance of AI without assuming that automation itself produces ethical or environmental improvement.

items.title: AI-supported first consultation preparation in oncology: a real-world clinical usability study
items.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) may support clinicians by facilitating information management, but their usability in real-world oncology practice remains understudied. This study evaluated the workflow performance of Artificial Intelligence-based First Consultation Preparation (AI-FCP), generating structured summaries from unstructured clinical documentation, co-created with end users. In a prospective single‑group pre‑post design, nine clinicians completed a person-level baseline, followed by 33 consultations with AI-FCP. Case numbers varied by clinic scheduling and enrollment timing, potentially introducing survivorship bias. Usability was evaluated using validated questionnaires and study-specific instruments. Post AI-FCP, overall perceived workload (NASA-TLX) was 28.9% lower than baseline (Hodges-Lehmann estimate difference −12.3; 95% CI –21.7 to –3.3), with self-reported average time savings of 3.26 min (SD = 2.65) per case. Preparation succeeded in 84.9% of consultations; 63.6% of summaries were complete. These exploratory findings suggest clinicians perceived lower workload and reported improved workflow efficiency with AI-FCP. Further research is needed to determine generalizability.

items.title: ALGORITHMIC GOVERNANCE AND CROSS-JURISDICTIONAL REGULATORY INTELLIGENCE: DOCTRINAL, ARCHITECTURAL, AND EMPIRICAL FOUNDATIONS
items.abstract: This study develops a jurisprudential, algorithmic, and systems framework for automated regulatory intelligence within the structurally fragmented administrative environment of the United States. Mechanical and HVAC regulation is used as a test domain because a single field operation may simultaneously implicate federal environmental rules, state licensing regimes, county or municipal permitting, locally adopted building codes, technician credentials, and address-specific inspection procedures. Comparative analysis of Illinois, Texas, North Carolina, and Arizona therefore treats the United States not merely as a geographical setting, but as an empirical governance laboratory for examining how artificial intelligence can mediate rules that vary by authority, location, and time. The analysis addresses three related problems. First, Home Rule, Dillon's Rule, and state preemption distribute local regulatory authority differently across the four states, creating materially different operational pathways (Baker & Rodriguez, 2009; Briffault, 2018; Briffault et al., 2020; Diller, 2017; Mead, 2019; Richardson, 2011; Stahl, 2024). Second, the federal HFC phasedown and EPA Technology Transitions program interact with state and local code-adoption cycles; this interaction may create sequencing gaps or administrative uncertainty, but it should not be characterized as a universal direct conflict or as a federal mandate to use one specific A2L refrigerant (U.S. EPA, 2026a, 2026b). Third, digitally generated compliance records require provenance, temporal reconstruction, qualified certification, and notice procedures if they are later offered under Federal Rules of Evidence 901 or 902(13)/(14); cryptographic hashing alone does not establish admissibility (Krishnamurthy, 2025; U.S. Courts, 2017). By combining constitutional and administrative analysis, point-in-polygon jurisdictional resolution, temporal knowledge graphs, constrained generative AI, human-in-the-loop governance, and cryptographic provenance, the study proposes a scalable research architecture rather than claiming a completed production platform. The U.S. HVAC case also provides a bridge to Metaverse governance: it demonstrates how physical territory can first become machine-readable, then algorithmically mediated, and comparable to an electronic jurisdiction in which digital space, identity, activity, and time determine the applicable governance regime (Kostenko et al., 2022, 2024, 2025).

items.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligent Scribes in Oncology: Impact on Clinician Experience and Documentation Burden
items.abstract: PURPOSE Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes, widely implemented to reduce clinician burden and dissatisfaction, are not optimized for oncology. We evaluated this technology at-scale at a high-volume cancer center. METHODS This prospective mixed-methods study used surveys, electronic health record (EHR), and utilization data to assess adoption, burden, and satisfaction with an ambient AI scribe that was implemented from June to September 2025. Descriptive statistics categorized clinicians as adopters (3+ weeks of use), attempted adopters (1-2 weeks), and never-users (0 weeks). Generalized estimating equations assessed the adoption's effect on the likelihood of closing notes on visit days and pajama time. Pre- and postimplementation surveys obtained clinicians' insights into satisfaction and documentation burden. RESULTS In all, 190 (19.8%) of 958 clinicians used the tool, most often with new, video, and in-person visits. Adopters (n = 124) and attempted adopters (n = 66) were more commonly physicians from medicine and surgery. Pre- to post-rollout, the likelihood of closing notes on visit days remained unchanged among never-users (70% v 70%) and decreased among attempted adopters (73% v 70%) and adopters (56% v 54%). Pajama time remained unchanged among attempted adopters (50.6 v 50.1 minutes per week) and decreased among never-users (69.5 v 62.2) and adopters (86.9 v 81.4). Clinicians completing both pre- and postrollout surveys (n = 45) showed a decrease in high/excessive note-writing time (78% v 60%; P = .043). Postrollout surveys (n = 77) showed largely positive experiences, with 73% reporting they would recommend the tool to colleagues. CONCLUSION This study of an ambient AI scribe at-scale showed positive satisfaction but mixed burden outcomes among oncology clinicians. Notably, despite enterprise-wide implementation and training, adoption was low and varied by clinician and visit characteristics. Future research should explore adoption barriers and tool optimization to support oncology documentation workflows.

items.title: An Adaptive Explainable AI Framework for Reliable Decision-making in Real-world Environments
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decisions in environments where data distributions, operational conditions, user needs, and risk levels change over time. Models that perform well during development may become unreliable after deployment because of data drift, concept drift, sensor degradation, population changes, or unexpected interactions. At the same time, predictive performance alone is insufficient for high-impact decisions: users need explanations that are understandable, relevant to the decision context, and accompanied by appropriate uncertainty information. This paper proposes an Adaptive Explainable AI (A-XAI) framework intended to integrate reliability monitoring, explanation generation, uncertainty estimation, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation within a unified lifecycle. The framework contains nine conceptual components: contextual data acquisition; data-quality, privacy, and drift assessment; prediction with uncertainty estimation; context-sensitive explanation generation; decision support and human oversight; risk-aware reliability gating; feedback and audit logging; controlled adaptation; and post-adaptation revalidation with version control. A formal decision policy is presented to connect predictive confidence, drift evidence, explanation quality, and consequence severity to actions such as automated recommendation, human review, abstention, or retraining. The paper also proposes an evaluation protocol spanning predictive performance, calibration, robustness, explanation fidelity and stability, fairness, latency, and operational outcomes. As a conceptual contribution, the framework is not presented as experimentally validated; its effectiveness must be tested in domain-specific studies using real deployment data and preregistered evaluation criteria. The proposed design offers a structured basis for developing AI systems that remain interpretable and risk-aware as real-world conditions evolve.

items.title: An Automated Exam Marking Framework using an Artificial Intelligence Tool for English Writing in General Foundation Program
items.abstract: This study proposes a fully automated exam marking framework for English writing in the General Foundation Program (GFP) through the use of prompt engineering with artificial intelligence (AI) tool ChatGPT and computer-based analysis. The AI tool generated 120 GFP B2 level writing responses (120 to 150 words each) with intentional grammatical errors. Four prompts were applied for automated marking by the AI tool as an examiner, based on a provided rubric, to detect errors, and awarding of a score [/10] (out of 10) to each response. A combination of different prompting techniques, including instruction-based, role-based, and formatting prompting were collectively used to design each prompt. All of the 120 responses were marked by each prompt. The first and second prompts were similar, just with a difference of paraphrasing. Prompts 3 and 4 were based on Prompt 2, containing only an addition of a single word for Prompt 3, and replacement of the added word with another word for Prompt 4. Statistical comparisons were done in SPSS. The Friedman test showed the similarities (Prompts 1 and 2 with paraphrased versions) and significant differences (Prompts 2, 3 and 4; p < .001, just due to an addition, and replacement of a single word) among the prompts outcomes based on the markings. Pairwise comparisons were performed using the Bonferroni correction to check for significant differences, while Kendall’s W test was used to measure the strength of agreement among the rankings. Human involvement in the study was limited to author-led validation of all the 120 responses, toward the accuracy of intentional added errors. The framework demonstrated how different prompts impacted the marking outcomes, which highlighted the sensitivity of the prompts to the addition of a single determinative word and the replacement of that word with another. Moreover, statistical comparisons showed how scalable assessment design and quality checks can be consistently applied for GFP English writing. This study showed that the proposed automated marking framework can support consistent, scalable, and prompt-sensitive assessment of GFP English writing.

items.title: An Integrated XAI-RL Architecture for Ethical Decision-Making in Autonomous Robots
items.abstract: Can a robot's ethical reasoning be transparent without slowing it down? That is the question we set out to answer. Autonomous robots now make decisions that affect people's lives, and if we cannot understand how they decide, trust becomes a serious problem. We built a unified architecture that couples Explainable AI (XAI) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) through three connected components: a Perception Layer for situational awareness, a Decision Reasoning Layer that breaks agent utility down into measurable ethical sub-rewards (safety, fairness, and well-being), and a contrastive Explainability Engine grounded in a real-time Ethical Ledger. We tested it against Black-Box RL and two post-hoc XRL baselines (LIME and SHAP) across two simulation environments and a physical robot pilot on a TurtleBot3 platform. Our system reached 92±3% ethical alignment in simulation and 89±4% on the physical platform, beating every baseline (p < 0.01 throughout). In a controlled, IRB-approved user study (N=128), participants rated it higher on trust (4.5±0.4), understandability (4.6±0.3), and perceived safety (4.4±0.5) than the alternatives. Explanations were also fast: 4.2±0.6 ms on average, versus 18.3±2.1 ms for SHAP and 12.7±1.8 ms for LIME on the same hardware—well within real-time limits. An ablation study and sensitivity analysis back up these architectural choices.

items.title: Analysis of Muscle Activation Patterns as Indicators of Gestures’ Ease of Use
items.abstract: Hand-based gestures are widely used in human-computer interaction but can cause muscle fatigue and discomfort that undermine long-term usability. This exploratory study examined whether gestures' ease of use can be reflected in distinct muscle activation patterns derived from surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. Twenty participants performed 32 predefined gestures while sEMG was recorded from eight forearm and upper-arm muscles, and rated each gesture's perceived effort on a 7-point scale. Gestures were grouped into high- and low-ease-of-use categories, and activation features were compared between groups. Results showed that high-ease-of-use gestures had significantly greater biceps activation, lower extensor carpi radialis activation, and reduced co-activation between the flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor digitorum superficialis. These findings suggest that ease of use relates to reduced motor complexity and reliance on proximal muscles, and demonstrate promise for sEMG in objectively indexing gestures' ease of use, offering insights to inform the design of more usable gesture-based interactions.
